<thought>We need the number of aromatic carbons in the molecule. The only way to infer that without a given structure is to examine the 13C NMR spectrum, which typically lists chemical shifts for each carbon. Aromatic carbons appear in the ~110‑160 ppm region. By retrieving the spectrum we can count how many signals fall in that range, giving the aromatic carbon count. This requires a single inexpensive measurement.</thought>
